summary: Learn blockchain and digital assets for finance with practical tools for treasury, custody, controls, and executive reporting.
lede: Digital-asset finance examines how tokenization and blockchain transactions intersect with treasury, payments, custody and settlement. For treasury, finance, payments and compliance professionals, the course builds practical skills in classifying assets, tracing transactions, reviewing smart-contract risks and evaluating custody controls. Exercises also help learners compare treasury use cases against settlement and governance needs, identify control gaps, and prepare findings for leadership.
audienceIntro: This blockchain and digital assets for finance course is designed for professionals who must evaluate digital-asset opportunities, manage control exposure, and explain implications to finance leadership.
prerequisites: Participants should have working knowledge of finance operations, treasury, payments, risk, compliance, or financial control processes. Prior blockchain coding or smart-contract development is not required, but you should be comfortable reading process maps, reviewing transaction data, and discussing control implications with technical and non-technical stakeholders. A laptop with internet access is required for practical exercises, and familiarity with spreadsheets will help you complete the analysis templates efficiently. For advanced discussion sections, the course assumes basic understanding of financial reporting, operational risk, AML/KYC concepts, and governance reporting. Coding is not required for completion. Advanced topics such as digital-asset infrastructure and smart-contract risk are taught at conceptual and operational application level, not technical engineering level.
